function: Predicts the excitation coefficients (beamforming vector, amplitude and phase) that maximize directivity or gain of a compact superdirective antenna array in a given direction (p. 3).
system: Four-element linear and 4x4 planar printed dipole arrays, spacing 0.10 to 0.50 wavelength, 1.6 GHz, modeled in CST; no RIS (p. 8, 11).
method: MultiTransUNet-GAN: U-Net generator with Transformer and global spatial attention plus CNN discriminator; supervised conditional GAN with NMSE term, offline training, warm-up cosine learning rate (p. 3-6, 10).
data_channel: Own CST full-wave simulation of dipole-array radiated fields, 5-degree sampling; labels from eigenvector solution of Eq. 6; 401 linear, 351 planar configurations; no standard channel (p. 8, 11).
test_conditions: 70% train, 30% test split of one CST dataset per array (linear, planar); capability for untrained spacings is asserted, with no held-out spacing test reported (p. 8, 9).
baselines: Non-learned: array theory-based, circuit theory-based, coupling-matrix-based beamforming and the theoretical value. Learned: TransUNet and the authors' MultiTransUNet ablation (p. 8, 9).
metrics: Directivity and array gain versus the theoretical value; NMSE (dB) and prediction accuracy of the excitation coefficients (p. 8-10).
complexity: Order O(Wm Hm Cm^2) for the generator; 2046.54 M FLOPs and 18.99 M parameters for MultiTransUNet-GAN (p. 7, 9).
q1_support: p. 8: "simulation software, CST". The fields come from the authors' own CST dipole-array simulation; no 3GPP, COST 2100 or DeepMIMO channel model and no measured data are used.
q2_support: p. 8: "split the datasets, using 70% for training and 30% for". The test set is a held-out part of the same CST data; p. 9 asserts "that have not been previously trained" spacings but reports no held-out spacing test.
q3_support: p. 9: "the array theory-based method and the circuit theory-based" and the coupling-matrix method are compared on directivity (Table III); p. 8: "the original TransUNet model, the proposed MultiTransUNet model" compared on prediction accuracy (Fig. 5, Table IV).
q4_support: p. 9: "model is about 2046.54 M". Table IV gives FLOPs and parameters, and Sec. III-C (p. 7) derives the order of complexity of the generator.
q5_support: p. 8: "The entire pipeline is implemented using PyTorch". No link or DOI to code or data is given, and the data are the authors' own CST simulations, not a public dataset.
notes: Borderline with the antenna hardware design exclusion; kept as area 3 because the network outputs the excitation (beamforming) vector of a fixed array, not the antenna structure (p. 3). TransUNet is the only learned baseline for q3: it is a separately published architecture [23] that the proposed generator extends, so it is counted as a standard architecture and not as an ablation; MultiTransUNet is an ablation and is not counted. The split is not stated to be by spacing, so q2 is 0; the reviewer may confirm the p. 9 sentence. PDF is the arXiv v2 preprint of the same paper.
